episodes.title: Glaucoma Is an Optic Neuropathy, Not Just High Eye Pressure
episodes.description:
Most people think glaucoma is simply a disease of high eye pressure — but that's only part of the story, and the incomplete picture could be putting your vision at risk. In this eye-opening episode of Focus Cast, we redefine glaucoma from the ground up and explain why it is, at its core, an optic neuropathy — a progressive disease that destroys the nerve fibers connecting your eye to your brain, causing permanent, irreversible vision loss.

We break down why elevated intraocular pressure is an important risk factor but not the defining feature of glaucoma, and why up to 30–40% of glaucoma patients have completely normal eye pressure. We also explore ocular hypertension — high pressure without nerve damage — and why it is not the same as glaucoma. You'll learn what a proper glaucoma evaluation actually involves, including optic nerve imaging, OCT scans, and visual field testing, and why relying on pressure readings alone can leave the real disease undetected.

We cover the key risk factors you need to know — age, family history, race, diabetes, high myopia, and more — and explain why glaucoma is called the silent thief of sight. Because by the time most people notice vision changes, significant nerve damage has already occurred.

Whether you've been diagnosed with glaucoma, have risk factors, or simply want to take your eye health seriously, this episode gives you the knowledge to ask better questions and act before it's too late.

Listen now, then visit Focuslinks.in for more eye health resources. If this episode helped you, share it — eye health conversations genuinely save vision.

episodes.title: Aqueous Humor: How Your Eye Produces and Drains Fluid
episodes.description:
What keeps your eye perfectly round and functioning as a precision optical instrument? The answer lies in a continuous fluid system most people never think about — until something goes wrong. In this episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we take a deep dive into aqueous dynamics, exploring how aqueous humor is produced, how it circulates through the eye, and how it drains through two remarkably different pathways.

We start with the ciliary body, where aqueous humor is actively secreted into the posterior chamber at a rate of two to three microliters per minute. From there, we follow the fluid as it flows through the pupil and into the anterior chamber, where it exits via the conventional trabecular meshwork pathway or the lesser-known uveoscleral pathway — a pressure-independent drainage route that runs through the ciliary muscle and suprachoroidal space before exiting through the sclera.

You will learn why the uveoscleral pathway was not even described in humans until the 1960s, how prostaglandin analogs like latanoprost and bimatoprost harness this pathway to treat glaucoma, and why this drainage route becomes less efficient as we age — raising the risk of elevated intraocular pressure and optic nerve damage. We also touch on cutting-edge surgical approaches, including micro-invasive glaucoma surgery devices targeting the suprachoroidal space.

Whether you are a healthcare professional, a student of ophthalmology, or simply someone who wants to understand how your eyes actually work, this episode delivers clear, science-backed insights in an accessible format. Listen now and see your eyes in a completely new way. Visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes on the science of vision.

episodes.title: Intraocular Pressure Explained: What That Number Really Means
episodes.description:
Your eye doctor reads out a number at every exam, says "looks good," and moves on — but do you actually know what intraocular pressure is, why it matters, and why it's never quite the same twice? In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down everything you need to know about IOP in plain, everyday language.

We start with the basics — what intraocular pressure is, how the eye maintains it through a fluid called aqueous humor, and what the normal range actually looks like. Then we get into the part most people never hear about: IOP fluctuates constantly. Time of day, body position, exercise, caffeine, even your sleeping habits can all shift that number in ways that matter, especially if you're at risk for glaucoma.

Speaking of glaucoma — we explain why elevated intraocular pressure is one of its biggest risk factors, why it's often called the silent thief of sight, and why catching it early through regular eye exams can make all the difference between preserved vision and permanent damage.

We also walk you through how IOP is actually measured, from the familiar air puff test to the gold standard Goldmann applanation tonometry, and touch on exciting new technologies on the horizon.

By the end of this episode, that number your eye doctor mentions won't just be background noise — it'll be something you understand, something you can ask smart questions about, and something you can actively help manage through everyday lifestyle choices.

If you care about protecting your vision for the long haul, this episode is for you. Visit us at Focuslinks.in to explore more eye health content from Focus Cast.

episodes.title: Pachymetry Correction: Why Corneal Thickness Changes Everything
episodes.description:
Is your eye pressure reading actually accurate? It might not be — and the answer lies in a thin, transparent structure just half a millimeter thick. In this episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we dive deep into central corneal thickness and the pachymetry correction, exploring one of the most clinically significant yet often overlooked variables in glaucoma diagnosis and management.

We break down how Goldmann applanation tonometry works, why its built-in assumptions about average corneal thickness can lead to dangerously misleading pressure readings, and what that means for real patients. You will learn how a cornea that is just 50 micrometers thicker or thinner than average can shift your intraocular pressure reading by 2.5 mmHg — enough to miss a glaucoma diagnosis entirely or trigger years of unnecessary monitoring.

We also cover the landmark Ocular Hypertension Treatment Study findings, the major pachymetry correction formulas including Ehlers and Doughty-Zaman, and why there is still no universal agreement on which formula to use. Plus, we explore how newer technologies like dynamic contour tonometry, ocular response analyzers, and corneal hysteresis measurements are reshaping how clinicians think about eye pressure beyond simple numbers.

Whether you are a patient wondering if your glaucoma risk has been properly assessed, a student building your clinical foundation, or a practitioner looking to sharpen your diagnostic thinking, this episode gives you the context to understand why pachymetry is not optional in modern eye care.

Listen now and visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes and vision science resources.
